# 金光明經

**ID:** T0663
**Volume:** T16
**Category:** 經集部類
**Original Category:** 經集部
**Byline:** 北涼 曇無讖譯
**Dynasty:** 北涼
**Date:** 414–426
**Juans:** 4
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T0663

## Contributors
- 曇無讖 (A001789)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

T663 is the earliest complete Chinese rendering of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra*, the *Sūtra of Golden Light*, in four fascicles and 19 chapters. Together with the *Lotus*, the *Vimalakīrti*, and the *Mahāparinirvāṇa*, it is one of the Mahāyāna sūtras with the deepest cultic and political impact in East Asia: its chapter on the Four Heavenly Kings (《四天王品》) made it the canonical scriptural ground for state-protective Buddhism (*hùguó* 護國) in China, Japan, and Korea, and its long ritual cycle of confession, dhāraṇī, and merit-transfer became liturgical bedrock.

**Abstract**

The translation is unanimously ascribed to [曇無讖](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%87%E7%84%A1%E8%AE%96) (Dharmakṣema, 385–433), produced at the Northern Liáng court of [沮渠蒙遜](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B2%AE%E6%B8%A0%E8%92%99%E9%81%9C) Jūqú Méngxùn in Gūzāng 姑臧. Date bracket follows Dharmakṣema's attested productive period at Gūzāng (414–426); the work was certainly complete by his death in 433. The text covers chapters 序品 through 囑累品 in 19 sections — including the famous *Confessions and Praises* (《懺悔品》 / 《讚歎品》), the Four Heavenly Kings cycle (chapters 6–10) which lays out the divine protection of any kingdom that recites the sūtra, the *Wángfǎ zhènglùn pǐn* "Right discourse on the Dharma of kingship" (《正論品》), and the closing Jātaka-style narratives (《流水長者子品》 *Elder Liúshuǐ's son*, 《捨身品》 *The Bodhisattva who gave his body to the tigress*).

T663 was supplemented by *[Hébù Jīnguāngmíng jīng 合部金光明經](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0302)* (T664) of [寶貴](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AF%B6%E8%B2%B4) (Sui, 597), which inserted four additional chapters into Dharmakṣema's frame from later partial translations by [真諦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E8%AB%A6) Paramārtha and [闍那崛多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%97%8D%E9%82%A3%E5%B4%9B%E5%A4%9A) Yaśogupta, and was eventually superseded for liturgical purposes by *[Jīnguāngmíng zuìshèngwáng jīng 金光明最勝王經](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0303)* (T665) of [義淨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E6%B7%A8) (Táng, 703), which is a fresh translation of the long Sanskrit recension in 31 chapters. Dharmakṣema's version remained, however, the version commented upon by the Tiāntái lineage from [智顗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E9%A1%97) onward (see [KR6i0306](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0306), [KR6i0307](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0307)) and by [吉藏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%89%E8%97%8F) in the Sānlùn lineage ([KR6i0308](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0308)).
